% note: Price basis: list price per answer. Study~1: the pre-registered price table, dated \mbox{2026-10-12}. Study~1b: its file gives the unit as US dollars per answer at list price and no price-table date. The Batch cost we paid is given where the files give it and is empty otherwise.
% note: Columns marked API count are counted from the usage records by free analysis 10, labelled ``post hoc; thinking tokens as the API reports them''. They are post hoc and have no interval. The thinking share of list cost is the thinking tokens priced at the model's list output rate, summed over the calls, divided by the summed list cost.
% note: Calls are the pre-specified counts: for Study~1 those recorded with its pre-specified thinking estimates, for Study~1b the Study~1b file's final count; free analysis 10 counts the same calls (checked when the table is built).
% note: Mean input and output tokens per answer are Study~1's pre-specified token means only for its Haiku-medium, Opus-medium and Sonnet-medium rows and its votes. Every other row's, including every Study~1b row's, are free analysis 10's (post hoc). Where both files hold a value they are equal (checked when the table is built).
% note: The two estimate columns are Study~1's pre-specified thinking estimates. Per call, visible tokens are estimated as the number of characters of the visible reply divided by 3, rounded down, and thinking tokens are the output tokens less that estimate, never below zero (the file's label: ``estimates (visible tokens~= characters / 3)''). They are biased: Haiku, thinking off gets 33.72\% / 34.53\% of its list cost as estimated thinking (chains / pieces), while the API counts a mean of 0.0 / 0.0 thinking tokens per call for it. The estimate stays as defined; the API columns are the thinking figures to read.
% note: Study~1b rows: format compliance is given per shape only (the files give none for a pooled row). A pooled row's calls are the Study~1b file's pooled count; free analysis 10 gives tokens per shape only, so the pooled rows' token cells are empty. Study~1's pre-specified thinking estimates do not apply to Study~1b (dash; the part of the table that gives Study~1b's token columns leaves those two columns out).
% note: Cost ratio is the setting's list cost per answer divided by Opus-medium's on the same shape. For Haiku-max per shape it is free analysis 10's ratio (post hoc; checked against the two recorded costs); for Study~1b's pooled Haiku-max row and the pooled Haiku-max vote it is the ratio recorded beside Tests~B1 and B2; elsewhere it is computed from the two recorded costs (post hoc arithmetic).
% note: Spend share of a vote: the vote's spend over its cost-matched comparator's. For the Study~1 votes it is the pre-registered $k$ file's, in Batch dollars; for the pooled Study~1b vote it is the ratio recorded beside Test~B2, at list price. The Study~1b file gives it for the pooled vote only, so its per-shape cells are the same quotient from the two recorded costs (post hoc arithmetic). A capped $k$ is held to the samples drawn, below its cost-matched $k$; its Setting cell gives both.
% note: A vote at $k$ costs $k$ answers; its cost per correct answer and accuracy are those of the vote. A Study~1 vote's Batch cost per answer is its spend in the pre-registered $k$ file ($k$ samples at the pre-specified Batch cost per sample; checked). A Study~1 vote's tokens per answer are those of its $k$ samples together (pre-specified); the Study~1b vote's are not given. Calls and thinking figures are not given for a vote (dash): it reuses its single samples, which are counted in their own rows. The format compliance shown for a vote is that of its single samples.
% note: Cells left empty are not given in the result files; a dash means the column does not apply.
% note: The vote at the cost-matched $k$ follows the pre-registered $k$ rule of each study. In Panel~1, each shape's own cost-matched $k$ at 16 steps is post hoc (free analysis 3), and so is the cost-matched $k$ at 6 steps and at 12 steps (free analysis 2: its $k$, the samples it is held to and its samples per comparator answer; the spend share is its vote cost over Opus-medium's, post hoc arithmetic). Neither changes a test, and no trend across lengths is read from them.
% note: Panel~2: per shape, the output-token and list-cost ratios are free analysis 10's ratios (post hoc); Study~1's Opus-medium tokens and both studies' costs are the pre-specified recorded values. The pooled rows give the list costs per answer and the ratio recorded beside Tests~B3 and B1. At 12 steps the Study~1b file gives no ratio, so it is computed from the two recorded costs (post hoc arithmetic); free analysis 2 gives its inverse (post hoc, Panel~1). No pooled output-token ratio is given.
% note: Panel~3: the Study~1b settings at 6 steps and 12 steps, with token figures counted by free analysis 10 (post hoc) and calls from the Study~1b file; the 16-step settings are in the main table. Panel~4: the trial round ran on separate sets; its step counts are those of the limits it set, and its list cost is the total over all of a setting's calls, not per answer.
